items.title: Building intelligent apps for Apple platforms with Claude in the Foundation Models framework
items.text: Today we're releasing Foundation Models framework support for Claude through a new Swift package that lets Apple developers use Apple's Foundation Models framework to call Claude for more complex workflows. Apple’s Foundation Models framework gives developers access to tap into models natively from Swift. It is very easy to use and can return typed Swift values through guided generation in as few as three lines of code. Developers can use this to tap into Apple’s on-device models for fast, local tasks like summarization or extraction. Developers can now use Apple’s Foundation Models framework to hand off to Claude when a request calls for multi-step reasoning, code generation, and more. items.title: I was curious how X is fighting AI slop, so I looked at its open-source algorithm
items.text: I was curious how X is fighting AI slop, so I looked at its open-source algorithm. It has a behavioral model called TweetSpamBot that analyzes up to 512 recent account actions, looking at signals like posting bursts, quote-post behavior, timing, and normal browsing or dwell between actions. The model is trained to recognize patterns such as: → TWEET_CREATE_BURST → QUOTE_TWEET_SPAMMER → CONTENT_AMPLIFIER A high score on the above can feed into an account challenge but doesn't seem to downrank the slop posts themselves. I think the gap here is that the model doesn’t read the actual post content. So a sophisticated AI content mill can still post slop all day long: 1. Find viral posts 2. Quote...

items.title: Making steam engines more efficient increased coal demand
items.text: Making steam engines more efficient increased coal demand. Higher-level languages made programming easier and resulted in far more software being built. Spreadsheets made financial analysis cheaper and resulted in businesses doing far more analysis. When the cost and complexity of a task falls, new use cases become economically viable. AI + software engineering will likely follow the same pattern: far more software solving far more problems, including problems that were previously economically unviable.
